content.text:
I've fixed the hydration warning. A repro test failed before the change and passes after it. The existing hydration and compiler-sfc tests still pass, and the type check is clean.

**Cause:** The repro uses `v-bind('props.backgroundColor')`. In dev builds, the SFC compiler escapes the `.` in that variable name, so the server writes `--xxx-props\.backgroundColor` into the style attribute. During hydration, `resolveCssVars` built the expected style from `instance.getCssVars()`, which returns the unescaped name `--xxx-props.backgroundColor`. The names don't match, so the check reported a mismatch.

The bug only appears together with a child style binding because the style comparison only runs when the child's root element has its own `style` prop (`:style="{ display }"`). Without it, nothing gets checked.

**Changes:**
- `packages/shared/src/escapeHtml.ts`: moved `getEscapedCssVarName` and `cssVarNameEscapeSymbolsRE` here from `compiler-sfc/src/script/utils.ts`, so the runtime can use them too.
- `packages/compiler-sfc/src/script/utils.ts`: now re-exports both from `@vue/shared`, so existing imports keep working.
- `packages/runtime-core/src/hydration.ts`: `resolveCssVars` now escapes each key the same way the compiler does before comparing.

I deleted the scratch repro test, so the fix doesn't come with a regression test.
